errors.quote: PersonaMem-v3 audits its data with LLM judges only
errors.paper_says: The PersonaMem-v3 data-quality verification section reports automated quality filters and a GPT-5.5 judge re-evaluation (96.6% pass rate), but also says "we also conduct qualitative human inspection ourselves to identify subtle data-quality issues and artifacts, iterating over a hundred of times". So the audit is not LLM-only; what is absent is a human study of judge accuracy.

errors.quote: A judge at 0.38 is therefore not far below the raters' own agreement
errors.paper_says: Minor, wrong direction: Re-Centering Humans gives inter-annotator Spearman 0.325 (p. 8) and the best judge 0.376 against the human average (p. 15, Table 6). The best judge is numerically above the human-human figure, not below it (the two are not like for like).

errors.quote: Spearman 0.61–0.74 across eleven judges on 200 responses
errors.paper_says: Minor: OP-Bench Table 5 (p. 14) gives 0.61–0.74 for Irrelevance only; Sycophancy runs 0.60–0.74 (DeepSeek-v3.2 = 0.60). The row is labelled as the over-personalisation score in general, so the range is 0.60–0.74. Eleven judges and 200 responses are correct.

asis-v2-q3-r2.review_only: its note records no human study of judge accuracy
asis-v2-q3-r2.comment: Broadest coverage of the three, and the only one to state the top-two swap (15) and CUPID (24). Pages and numbers check out for Re-Centering, PRISM-X, PersonaLens, LaMP-QA, CUPID and Semantic Constraint Verification. Points counted leniently: 4 has no deltas and no Claude over-penalisation; 9 has no 367 ratings or Prolific; 14 gives 33.8%/15.0% without the human ~25% baseline; 13 gives only the Sim-Judgement condition. The PersonaMem-v3 line leans on a note rather than the paper and is partly wrong. The library-wide claims ('Only PRISM-X has the person being personalised for do the judging', 'Nothing in the library has users judge answers ... over time') were not checked.

asis-v2-q3-r1.review_only: The calibration advice comes from the evaluation review's "Calibrating the judge against people" section; I did not re-read its source papers.
asis-v2-q3-r1.comment: No wrong statement found; every number and page I checked holds: Re-Centering p. 6 (κ 0.300/0.426/0.597, 20% vs 40–60%), p. 8, p. 9 and p. 15 Table 6; PersonaLens Table 5 including 0.865; LaMP-QA p. 7 and p. 10; PRISM-X p. 16–17; Semantic Constraint Verification Table 3 and p. 9; HorizonBench p. 7 (56–64% majority-vote accuracy); and the skipped.yaml entry for 'Can LLM be a Personalized Judge?' (2406.11657, reason says narrow). The only answer to cover Stage 2 relevance matching (7). The OP-Bench range '0.60–0.68 for the five judges I read' is literally true of the first five rows and openly hedged, but understates the table (eleven judges, best 0.74); counted as 26 leniently. Omits 54.6%, the reward-model result, judge-size inflation and position bias. 9 counted on 'three third-party raters on 80 items'. The practical advice (calibrate on a few hundred human labels) is flagged as resting on a review, not checked in papers.

asis-v2-q3-r3.review_only: its line that LLM judges call generic answers personalised (Semantic Constraint Verification) rests on 8B-class judges. [...] I did not re-read its Table 3.
asis-v2-q3-r3.comment: No wrong statement found. Verified: PrefEval p. 43 Table 18 (0.92–0.97 is the final-accuracy row; per-checker is 0.86–0.98); OP-Bench Table 5 (0.68 GPT-4o-mini, 0.74 best); PersonaLens Table 5; Re-Centering p. 8 (54.6%, Δ 0.03 and −0.39), p. 9 and p. 15 (80 items, 367 ratings, 3.41–4.02 vs 3.18); LaMP-QA p. 7 and p. 10; PRISM-X p. 16–18 (44.9% vs 7.2% is the Sim-Dynamic condition). The only answer with PrefEval (23) and with the full point 4 deltas. 14 counted leniently (no human ~25% baseline); 28 counted leniently: it gives the claim and the limitation (p. 9) but no 0–19% figure, attributes the claim to the review, and says Table 3 was not re-read. That sits slightly at odds with 'every number below was checked in the paper itself', though no unchecked number is actually quoted.
